Quantum Business Solutions for Digital Monitoring Products

Same site. Three ways to design it.

Each one is the whole site, not a home page and two mockups: every page is built and live in all three. The words are the same in all three and the composition is not, so the decision in front of you is about direction, not copy. Open any one, then use the switcher pinned to the bottom of the page to flip between all three without losing your place.

Your call

Three directions. Your call.

The words and the pages are the same in all three. What differs is the register. Open each one and tell us which feels like DMP.

How to choose

Showcase: image-led

Layered photography and a sales-forward feel. It makes the most of DMP's product and facility photos.

Clean: plain and fast

High contrast, product names first. Built for dealers and specifiers scanning for a panel or module.

Press: editorial

Serif headings and a magazine feel, so a 50-year-old manufacturer reads like the established name it is.

Search and AI answers

Where you stand in search today, and what changes

Measured before we touched anything, so the work can be judged against it.

23,660organic visits a month, worth $248,538 a month in paid equivalent

Top findings, ranked by what they cost

1
Critical

DMP is not in the top ten for any of the national category searches dealers and specifiers run

Evidence
Seven category searches were checked in Semrush's US database on 9 November 2026. DMP is not in the top ten for any of them. Its best positions are 22 for 'alarm panel' (1,300 a month, difficulty 20) and 42 for 'access control panel' (480 a month, difficulty 16). It has no top-100 position for 'fire alarm control panel' (5,400 a month, difficulty 24), 'wireless alarm system' (1,300, difficulty 46), 'commercial access control system' (720, difficulty 30) or 'security keypad' (320, difficulty 13), and sits at 35 for 'cellular alarm communicator' (70, difficulty 0). Who holds the top spots: buildings.honeywell.com at 1 for 'fire alarm control panel', adiglobaldistribution.us at 1 for 'access control panel', hanwhavision.com at 1 and avigilon.com at 2 for 'commercial access control system', alarmgrid.com at 1 for 'alarm panel' and for 'cellular alarm communicator'. Where DMP does win is its own cellular communicator page: 'cell communicator' (260 a month) at 3 and 'alarm system cellular communicator' (110) at 4.
What it costs
A dealer or specifier who does not yet know DMP and searches by category meets Honeywell, Axis, Avigilon, the distributors and the parts retailers instead. DMP's category pages exist, at /products/control-panels and /products/access-control, but they rank 22nd and 42nd.
What we do
Give each product category a page written as the answer to the buyer's search (what it is, which listings and certifications apply, how it connects, which model fits), with question headings, FAQPage markup and links down to the products. In the build, starting with panels, access control, fire and communicators.
2
Medium

No test yet of whether AI assistants name DMP for national buyer questions

Evidence
The September local test is withdrawn because it measured local installers, not the dealers and specifiers DMP sells through. A national test has not been run yet. The questions we will put to an assistant with web search are the ones a dealer or specifier would ask: which manufacturers make a UL-listed commercial intrusion panel with cellular communication, which access control panel works with mobile credentials, which fire alarm control panel is listed for commercial use, which alarm communicators support dual-path reporting, and which manufacturers sell only through dealers. What is measured today is the sources an assistant would read: the top ten Google results for seven national category searches, listed in the AI answer section below, are led by buildings.honeywell.com, adiglobaldistribution.us, alarmgrid.com, avigilon.com and axis.com. dmp.com is in none of those top tens.
What it costs
Until the test is run the honest position is that we do not know. What we do know is that the pages an assistant would be reading for these questions belong to other companies, and that dmp.com carries no Product, FAQPage or sameAs markup to help an engine attribute an answer to DMP.
What we do
Run the national question set against an assistant with web search before day 30 and record the answers and the sources read. Meanwhile build the category pages, FAQPage markup, Product markup and sameAs links that give an engine something to read and attribute. In the build, with the test in the first 30 days.
3
High

The front door takes three hops, and robots.txt answers 404

Evidence
https://dmp.com/ answers 301 to http://www.dmp.com/, which then answers 307, a temporary redirect, rather than one permanent redirect to https. https://www.dmp.com/robots.txt returns HTTP 404 although the file holds rules and two Sitemap lines; crawlers treat a 4xx robots file as no file, so the rules and the sitemap declaration are never read. The XML sitemap itself is live at /sitemaps-1-sitemap.xml and lists 369 products, 26 categories and 197 pages, and a second Sitemap line points at a gforce.www.dmp.com host.
What it costs
Search engines and AI crawlers that start at the apex or over http make extra hops, one of them temporary, and the file meant to steer them and declare the sitemap is ignored. DMP's crawl policy is whatever the 404 implies, not a decision.
What we do
Serve every address variant with one permanent 301 to https://www.dmp.com/, return robots.txt with a 200, declare the sitemap in it, name the AI crawlers and drop the gforce line. In the build, week one.
4
High

Organization markup exists, but nothing describes the products, the questions or the profiles

Evidence
Of 241 pages audited, 226 carry Organization, WebPage and BreadcrumbList markup with the headquarters address, phone number and founding date. None carries Product, ItemList or FAQPage markup, none has a sameAs link, and none declares a contact point (0 of 241), although DMP publishes four support lines with hours. The most specific type on a product page is WebPage.
What it costs
Search engines and answer engines know who DMP is, but not what the 369 products are, which questions they answer or which LinkedIn, YouTube and Crunchbase profiles belong to the company, so they fall back on Indeed, Glassdoor and Reddit for the brand and on distributors for the products.
What we do
Add Product markup from the product table to every product page, ItemList to the category pages, FAQPage and CollectionPage to the system pages, a ContactPoint for each support line, and sameAs links to LinkedIn, YouTube and Crunchbase. Keep the Springfield headquarters address in the Organization markup as it is. In the build.
5
High

Three quarters of the traffic is people who already know the brand

Evidence
Semrush's intent split for dmp.com on 9 November 2026 puts 17,705 of 23,660 monthly visits, 75 percent, in navigational searches. The top organic term is 'dmp' at 9,900 a month, bringing 7,920 visits, a third of all traffic on its own, followed by 'digital monitoring products' at 880 and a long list of part numbers and product names: 'dmp support' 590, 'dmp keypad' 480, 'dmp xr550' 260, 'dmp 734' 260. Non-navigational traffic is 5,955 visits a month. The one high-volume non-branded term among the leading pages is 'white on white paper' at 12,100 a month in the September pull, position 9, which lands on the JamAlert white paper and has nothing to do with security.
What it costs
The site harvests existing dealers and customers looking up model numbers and support logins. It does not introduce DMP to anyone who has not already heard the name, so the whole top of the funnel depends on trade shows, reps and word of mouth.
What we do
Build the eight system pages and a resource hub that target category language rather than part numbers, starting with access control and fire. In the build for the pages, 90-day plan for the content programme.

Today Semrush US database and live HTML, 9 November 2026

  • Semrush shows dmp.com with 7,521 organic keywords and 23,660 organic visits a month in the US database, valued at $248,538 a month in equivalent paid traffic, and zero paid keywords running.
  • 75 per cent of that organic traffic is navigational: "dmp" alone at 9,900 a month brings a third of it. For seven national category searches, such as fire alarm control panel and access control panel, DMP is not in the top ten.
  • The home page is sound on the basics (title, one H1, canonical, 628 words, a phone link, a form and Organization markup) and still scores 52 of 100. Across 241 public pages the average is 35 and none scores above a D.
  • https://www.dmp.com/robots.txt answers HTTP 404 although it holds rules and Sitemap lines, so crawlers ignore it. The sitemap is live, and the apex takes a 301 to http://www.dmp.com/ and then a 307.
  • The pages that earn the visits are product and support pages: the home page takes 49.01 per cent of organic traffic across 209 keywords, the dealer admin page 3.52 per cent, the 734 access module page 2.93 per cent and the control panels index 2.63 per cent.
  • No page carries Product, FAQPage, ContactPoint or sameAs markup. 175 of 241 pages have fewer than 300 words and 107 share one default description.

After launch

  • Every URL answers once, at one canonical host, with a working robots.txt and a declared sitemap.
  • Eight system pages, each with question headings and a FAQ marked up as FAQPage.
  • Product, ItemList and ContactPoint markup, with sameAs links to the company's profiles and the headquarters address in the Organization markup.
  • Category pages for panels, access control, fire and communicators written as the answer to the dealer's or specifier's search.
  • A title, description, alt text and real copy on every product page, generated from the product table.

What we do not promise: Rankings and traffic depend on the market and on what you publish after launch. What we promise is that nothing about the build is the reason they do not come, that every number is re-measured at 30, 60 and 90 days, and that you see the same report we do.

Site-wide checks

  • Yes The site is served over HTTPS, and HSTS is set.
  • No https://dmp.com/ answers 301 to http://www.dmp.com/, which answers 307, a temporary redirect, instead of one permanent redirect to https://www.dmp.com/.
  • No robots.txt answers HTTP 404 although it holds rules and two Sitemap lines, so crawlers ignore it.
  • Yes An XML sitemap is live at /sitemaps-1-sitemap.xml and lists 369 products, 26 categories and 197 pages.
  • Yes GPTBot, ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, Bingbot and Googlebot all reach the site, but only because the robots file is ignored, not because it grants access.
  • No llms.txt is not published (the address returns 404).
  • Yes Organization markup with the address, phone number and founding date is present on 226 of 241 pages audited.
  • No Product, ItemList, FAQPage and ContactPoint markup are absent on all 241 pages, and there are no sameAs links.
  • No 137 of 241 pages share one default Open Graph image, so shared links look identical.
  • No 107 of 241 pages share one default meta description.
  • Yes Canonical tags are present on 226 of 241 pages audited; 15 pages returned an unusual response during the crawl and need a re-check.
  • Yes No accidental noindex: 0 of 241 pages are blocked from search.
  • No Words per page: median 174, and 175 of 241 pages have fewer than 300 words.
  • No 226 of 241 pages have at least one image with no alt attribute.

What we are treating as fixed

What your site and brand profile already say

There is no design brief from DMP yet. This version is written from dmp.com itself, read on 9 November 2026: its history, certifications, support lines, product catalogue, news and photography, in DMP's own words wherever a claim is DMP's to make. Tell us where it is wrong; your words outrank ours.

  • DMP sells through authorized dealers and distributors, so the site's first job is dealers and specifiers: find the product, get the spec sheet, place the order, reach a person.
  • DMP is a current Quantum client with a HubSpot CRM, marketing, sales and service launch under way, so the site has to feed that: forms that create records and one place for dealers to start.
  • DMP's own brand is yellow, black and beige. The previews use that palette, DMP's real logo and DMP's own photography, so what you see is closer to the finished site than a mood board.

What we found

And what we would do about it

  • Search (Semrush US database, 9 November 2026): about 23,660 organic visits a month on 7,521 keywords, but 75 percent of that is navigational, people already searching the brand. DMP is not in the top ten for any of seven national category searches such as fire alarm control panel and access control panel. An AI-answer test on national buyer questions has not been run yet.
  • A page-level audit of 241 public pages on www.dmp.com (9 November 2026) averages 35 out of 100, and no page scores above a D. The home page is the strongest at 52: it has a title, one H1, a canonical, a phone link and a form.
  • The front door and the robots file: https://dmp.com/ answers 301 to http://www.dmp.com/, which answers 307. robots.txt returns HTTP 404 although it holds rules and Sitemap lines, so crawlers ignore it. The sitemap is live (369 products, 26 categories, 197 pages), and there is no llms.txt.
  • Markup: Organization (address, phone, founding date) is on 226 of 241 pages. None carries Product, ItemList, FAQPage or ContactPoint markup, and there are no sameAs links.
  • Page content: 175 of 241 pages have under 300 words, 107 share one default description, 66 titles are under 25 characters, 226 pages have an image with no alt text, and only 36 have a question heading.
  • Correction to the September report: its crawl started at the redirecting apex and read one URL, so its findings about the home page's title, H1, canonical, robots.txt, sitemap and structured data were wrong for the real site. They are replaced here.
  • Strengths to keep: 50 years of history, a real manufacturing story, SOC 2 Type II examinations, 14 product categories, a deep library of spec sheets and guides, and 1,916 referring domains.

To confirm with you

Ten things we wrote as a draft, not a fact

Each of these appears on the pages. None is built until you confirm or correct it.

  • How the product catalogue is built. dmp.com has hundreds of product pages (the sitemap lists panels, keypads, modules, readers, cameras and accessories by part number). HubSpot's page limits depend on the tier, so we need DMP's tier before deciding between building every product page in HubSpot and keeping the catalogue on its current system behind the new front door.
  • The promise line. The home page says 'Security systems, built in Springfield', which is DMP's founding story, not a confirmed tagline.
  • Typefaces. DMP uses Gotham. The previews use the Quantum theme typefaces; Gotham needs a licence for the real site.
  • Photography and logos. Images come from dmp.com, as does the logo. They are used here for a private preview. Confirm rights, and supply anything newer.
  • Milestone details. The timeline repeats DMP's own history list. Photos beside 1975, 1993, 2005, 2021 and 2025 come from dmp.com's history and about pages; confirm the years against the originals.
  • Claims taken from DMP's own announcements: the XR Series being 32 times faster, the XR650 award, JamAlert's UL certification, and the jewelry store coverage mentioned in the JamAlert graphic. Each needs DMP's approval before it goes live in a headline.
  • Industries. All eleven pages are written from DMP's own industry pages (dmp.com/products/industries). Quotations are condensed; each featured product, white paper and compliance claim (for example UL 634 Level 2, NDAA/TAA, FirstNet approval, 256-bit AES) needs DMP's approval before it is repeated in a headline.
  • Social profiles. None are linked on dmp.com, so none appear. We recommend adding LinkedIn, YouTube and Crunchbase to the markup.
  • Dealer routes. A dealer locator, a become-a-dealer path and a dealer login were not found on dmp.com, so none are drawn. Confirm what dealers and specifiers need to start.
  • The associations strip. The logos are those shown on dmp.com's About page. Confirm membership status for each before showing them as a row of badges.
  • The apex redirect, the gforce.www.dmp.com sitemap line and the buy.dmp.com ordering site are out of scope for the front-end build but affect search and the hand-off.
  • The audit covers 241 public pages (156 of the page sitemap, 129 of 369 products and 28 category pages, with the dealer-facing intranet pages left out), because DMP's firewall blocks our audit agent. Ask DMP IT to allow our crawler so we can audit every page and run the site checks properly; until then the site-level results come from individual requests.
  • Images come from each product's og:image on dmp.com. The XR650 image carries a burned-in COMING SOON banner and the VUE Plus 7061, 7121 and 7081 images are cropped on a black background; DMP should supply clean product shots.
  • The XR650 is marked coming soon on dmp.com; confirm whether the page should stay live, and add release timing if known. FIPS 140-3, 802.1x and Active Directory features are marked as available with licenses.
  • VUE Plus 7121-FE shares the 7061-FE product photo on dmp.com; DMP to supply a 12MP-specific image if one exists.
  • XTLplus and XTLtouch share one product photo, Entré Lite and Entré Enterprise share one photo, and the 5-inch and 9800 keypad pages share one photo on dmp.com.
  • Library entries list documents named on dmp.com (spec sheets, guides, compliance notes, firmware release notes) as plain text because the preview cannot link PDFs. DMP to confirm which should be linked or gated on the live site.
  • Panel specification values for XT50, XR150, XR550, XTLplus and XTLtouch come from the six-panel comparison table on dmp.com. The XR150FC and XR550FC pages carry no table of their own, so none is shown.
  • The 7-inch touchscreen keypad page says the 8862 and 8863 are available, while a firmware note on the same page says they are available for preorder; DMP to confirm current availability.
  • The 5-inch touchscreen keypad page (7800 Series) describes a wireless display in its feature text although it covers wired 7872, 7873 and 7883 models; the copy here says 5-inch touchscreen only. DMP to confirm.
  • The XT50 table lists 42 hardwired zones while the feature text gives 10 onboard plus 32 wired; both are consistent but DMP should confirm which to lead with.
  • SCS-VR page carries dealer support billing FAQs with 2022 and 2023 dates; only evergreen billing facts are used. DMP to confirm the page should keep them.

  • All forms (quote request, dealer application, Marketing Central sign-up, private label, lead form) are placeholders until the HubSpot forms are wired. The field lists on get-a-quote and become-a-dealer come from the fields on the current dmp.com forms; the option lists for business type, major markets and annual revenue were not reproduced.

Where the two disagreed the newer category page was used: key fobs on XR panels use zones 400-449 (older page said 401-449); the wireless transmitter LED test follows the category page (five consecutive blinks, LED on about 8 seconds when faulty) rather than the older 'more than one second' wording; keypad firmware downloads are on the Product Software Downloads page (older page said Dealer Direct Software Downloads). The plan

From a choice to a live site

Days 1 to 10

Serve the site at one canonical host with a single HTTPS 301, name the crawlers in robots.txt, publish llms.txt, and add sameAs links to the Organization markup, which keeps the headquarters address as it is.

Days 10 to 30

Confirm the items below, decide how the product catalogue is built (see the first item), and sign off copy for each of the eight system lines.

Days 30 to 45

Build the eight system pages with question headings, FAQ markup, product lists and an enquiry form on each.

Days 45 to 60

Build the about and proof pages, and add Product markup to the catalogue pages.

Days 60 to 90

Publish the first three answer posts against access control, fire alarm and video surveillance questions, and the news and resources hub.

Day 90

Re-run the same national keyword set, the same AI questions and the same page audit against the baseline.
